<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Generation">Generation</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=1&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Generation" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section's source code: Generation"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Trees can only generate on supported blocks (see <a href="#Growth_and_Characteristics"><span style="white-space: nowrap;">§ Growth and Characteristics</span></a>). Tree placement from one biome can slightly overlap into neighboring biomes.
</p><p><a href="/w/Fallen_tree" class="mw-redirect" title="Fallen tree">Fallen trees</a> and <a href="/w/Trees_with_vines" class="mw-redirect" title="Trees with vines">trees with vines</a>‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">BE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> generate wherever their regular variants generate, with a few exceptions.
</p><p><b><span class="nowrap"><span class="sprite-file" style=""><span class="pixel-image" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/w/Oak" title="Oak"><img alt="" src="/images/EnvSprite_oak.png?742a4" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="16" height="16" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="16" data-file-height="16"></a></span></span><a href="/w/Oak" title="Oak"><span class="sprite-text">Oak</span></a></span></b>:
</p>
<ul><li><span class="nowrap"><span class="sprite-file" style=""><span class="pixel-image" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/w/Forest" title="Forest"><img alt="" src="/images/BiomeSprite_forest.png?98e29" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="16" height="16" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="16" data-file-height="16"></a></span></span><a href="/w/Forest" title="Forest"><span class="sprite-text">Forest</span></a></span> – high density; with <a href="/w/Leaf_litter" class="mw-redirect" title="Leaf litter">leaf litter</a></li>
<li><span class="nowrap"><span class="sprite-file" style=""><span class="pixel-image" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/w/Flower_Forest" title="Flower Forest"><img alt="" src="/images/BiomeSprite_flower-forest.png?d1802" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="16" height="16" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="16" data-file-height="16"></a></span></span><a href="/w/Flower_Forest" title="Flower Forest"><span class="sprite-text">Flower Forest</span></a></span> – medium high density; no fallen oaks</li>
<li><span class="nowrap"><span class="sprite-file" style=""><span class="pixel-image" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/w/Wooded_Badlands" title="Wooded Badlands"><img alt="" src="/images/BiomeSprite_wooded-badlands.png?9802c" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="16" height="16" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="16" data-file-height="16"></a></span></span><a href="/w/Wooded_Badlands" title="Wooded Badlands"><span class="sprite-text">Wooded Badlands</span></a></span> – medium density only on plateaus or near rivers; no fancy oaks; with <a href="/w/Leaf_litter" class="mw-redirect" title="Leaf litter">leaf litter</a></li>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Structure">Structure</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=2&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Structure" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section's source code: Structure"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Trees_preview.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Trees_preview.png/300px-Trees_preview.png?70301" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Trees_preview.png/600px-Trees_preview.png?70301 2x" data-file-width="3840" data-file-height="2160"></a><figcaption>Some trees grown from saplings</figcaption></figure>
<p>Trees vary widely in height, from a bare minimum of 1 log block for jungle bushes, ranging up to a maximum of 30 blocks for mega jungle trees.
</p><p>Tree canopies are composed of <a href="/w/Leaves" title="Leaves">leaf blocks</a> and grow 1 block higher than the highest <a href="/w/Log" title="Log">log block</a> (except those of the fancy oak, whose leaves grow 3 blocks higher). The canopy may begin from the ground and go up to 6 blocks from the ground. Tree canopies are generated from roughly spherical clusters of leaves about 5–7 blocks across, centered on sections of trunk or branches. Leaves must be supported by an adjacent trunk (or leaf blocks connected to the trunk); otherwise, they disappear.
</p><p>Fancy oak, dark oak, mangrove, azalea, cherry, pale oak, acacia, and mega jungle trees grow branches (logs connected horizontally, vertically, or diagonally to the trunk or other branches). Most of the time, a single tree has between one and six branches, and each branch has between one and six <a href="/w/Log" title="Log">logs</a>.​<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><a href="/w/Special:TalkPage/Tree" title="Special:TalkPage/Tree"><span title="How do acacia branches work?" style="border-bottom: 1px dotted">more information needed</span></a></i>]</sup> Regular oak and regular jungle trees lack branches, as do all variants of birch and spruce.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Growth_and_characteristics">Growth and characteristics</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=3&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Growth and characteristics" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section's source code: Growth and characteristics"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Jungle_tree_growth_example.png" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="/images/thumb/Jungle_tree_growth_example.png/300px-Jungle_tree_growth_example.png?6e16a" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="210" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Jungle_tree_growth_example.png/600px-Jungle_tree_growth_example.png?6e16a 2x" data-file-width="844" data-file-height="592"></a><figcaption>This jungle tree cannot grow because of the red wool block (looking southeast from the northwestern corner).</figcaption></figure>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">See also: <a href="/w/Tutorial:Tree_farming" title="Tutorial:Tree farming">Tutorial:Tree farming</a> 
</div>
<p>Trees are created when <a href="/w/Chunk" title="Chunk">chunks</a> are generated, and can also be grown from <a href="/w/Sapling" title="Sapling">saplings</a>.
</p><p>Tree saplings have a <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>20</sub> chance (<sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>40</sub> if they are jungle saplings) of dropping from <a href="/w/Leaf" class="mw-redirect" title="Leaf">leaf</a> blocks when they decay or are destroyed. There are eight species of saplings, corresponding to eight trees: oak, birch, spruce, jungle, acacia, dark oak, cherry and pale oak.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:UndergroundTree.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/UndergroundTree.png/300px-UndergroundTree.png?54c3e" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/UndergroundTree.png/600px-UndergroundTree.png?54c3e 2x" data-file-width="1366" data-file-height="768"></a><figcaption>A tree that was grown in a cave, with the necessary light provided by <a href="/w/Torch" title="Torch">torches</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The sapling can be planted on any variant of <a href="/w/Dirt" title="Dirt">dirt</a>, (except <a href="/w/Dirt_path" class="mw-redirect" title="Dirt path">dirt path</a>) a <a href="/w/Moss_block" class="mw-redirect" title="Moss block">moss block</a>, or <a href="/w/Mud" title="Mud">mud</a>, and must have a <a href="/w/Light" title="Light">light</a> level of at least 8 in the sapling block. 
</p><p>A sapling uproots with light level 7 or less in the sapling block itself unless it has a view of the sky that is unobstructed (except by <a href="/w/Glass" title="Glass">glass</a> or <a href="/w/Opacity" title="Opacity">other transparent materials</a>). The sapling must have at least 6 blocks of space above it to grow; the amount of required space varies between the different species of trees. A ceiling above sapling limits the <i>maximum</i> height of the tree that can grow from that sapling. However, dirt blocks and logs may not prohibit tree growth, and in some cases may be replaced as a sapling attempts to grow through them. However in <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, logs prohibit tree growth.
</p><p>If multiple saplings are planted next to each other, each one grows as long as the leaves from the other grown saplings do not block too much of the sunlight. Artificial light (torches, etc.) can still be used to grow them if this happens.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:CaveTree.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/CaveTree.png/300px-CaveTree.png?23ca0" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/CaveTree.png/600px-CaveTree.png?23ca0 2x" data-file-width="854" data-file-height="480"></a><figcaption>Trees can be generated anywhere where there is light and dirt in the Overworld.</figcaption></figure>
<p>All trees in the active <a href="/w/Chunk" title="Chunk">chunk</a> radius around the player make attempts to grow at random intervals. For any given tree this can work out to about one growth attempt per minute. When a tree attempts to grow, it first checks that it has enough light, then randomly chooses which variant of that species of tree to become; for example, an oak sapling chooses to grow as either a normal or fancy oak.
</p><p>Once a tree has passed a light check and chosen size to attempt, it checks if there is enough space for its chosen size. If it encounters an obstruction during this check, it fails to grow and must wait for the next pass before it can attempt to grow again. This means that a tree in an open field with enough light grows relatively quickly, but a tree in a cramped tree farm that stunts its size may make several attempts before finally growing.
</p><p><a href="/w/Bone_meal" class="mw-redirect" title="Bone meal">Bone meal</a>, when <span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">used</span> on a <a href="/w/Sapling" title="Sapling">sapling</a>, has a chance of forcing it to grow, so long as all of the normal checks (light, space, dirt, etc.) have passed. It does not <i>guarantee</i> growth, but forces an <i>attempt</i> to grow.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:NetherTrees.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/NetherTrees.png/300px-NetherTrees.png?cfd6a" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/NetherTrees.png/600px-NetherTrees.png?cfd6a 2x" data-file-width="1366" data-file-height="768"></a><figcaption>Planting trees in the <a href="/w/The_Nether" title="The Nether">Nether</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>All saplings grow normally in <a href="/w/The_Nether" title="The Nether">the Nether</a> and in <a href="/w/The_End" title="The End">the End</a>, although they must be planted in <a href="/w/Dirt" title="Dirt">dirt</a> transported from the <a href="/w/Overworld" title="Overworld">Overworld</a> and provided with sufficient light and space. Leaf blocks in the Nether have the same color as if they were placed in a <a href="/w/Desert" title="Desert">desert</a> biome. In the End, they are a dull bluish-green, as in the <a href="/w/Windswept_hills" class="mw-redirect" title="Windswept hills">windswept hills</a> biome.
</p><p>In order to grow a 2×2 tree (be it <a href="/w/Spruce" title="Spruce">spruce</a>, <a href="/w/Jungle_Tree" title="Jungle Tree">jungle</a>, <a href="/w/Dark_Oak" title="Dark Oak">dark oak</a>, or <a href="/w/Pale_Oak" title="Pale Oak">pale oak</a>), four saplings must be placed adjacent to each other in a square. For growth to succeed, there must be no <a href="/w/Block" title="Block">blocks</a> adjacent (even diagonally) to the north-western side up to the final height of the tree. The <a href="/w/Bone_meal" class="mw-redirect" title="Bone meal">bone meal</a> can be used on any of the <a href="/w/Sapling" title="Sapling">saplings</a>. The largest <a href="/w/Jungle_Tree" title="Jungle Tree">mega jungle trees</a>, <a href="/w/Spruce" title="Spruce">mega spruces</a>, and <a href="/w/Pine" class="mw-redirect" title="Pine">mega pines</a> reach 31 blocks tall. Dark oaks are typically 6–8 blocks tall.
</p><p><a href="/w/Leaves" title="Leaves">Leaves</a> and <a href="/w/Log" title="Log">logs</a> removed from a tree do not grow back over time.
</p><p>When a sapling on a <a href="/w/Grass_Block" title="Grass Block">grass block</a> or <a href="/w/Mycelium" title="Mycelium">mycelium</a> or <a href="/w/Moss_Block" title="Moss Block">moss block</a> grows into a tree, the block the <a href="/w/Sapling" title="Sapling">sapling</a> was planted on is instantly converted to dirt.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Types_of_trees">Types of trees</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=4&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Types of trees" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section's source code: Types of trees"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">See also: <a href="/w/Tree/Structure" title="Tree/Structure">Tree/Structure</a> 
</div>
<p>There are ten trees with a unique sapling. Most trees have different variants, some of which cannot be grown.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Oak">Oak</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=5&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Oak" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section's source code: Oak"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Oak" title="Oak">Oak</a></div>
<p>Oaks are among the most common trees in the game. They have the smallest space requirements, and along with <a href="/w/Dark_oak" class="mw-redirect" title="Dark oak">dark oak</a> trees, they can drop an <a href="/w/Apple" title="Apple">apple</a> when a leaf block is destroyed. In <a href="/w/Swamp" title="Swamp">swamp</a> biomes, a slightly larger variant of the regular oak with <a href="/w/Vines" title="Vines">vines</a> called the swamp oak is generated, which can naturally generate in shallow <a href="/w/Water" title="Water">water</a>. Fancy oaks may also grow or generate in place of regular oaks; these are taller and may feature branches. A rare variant is its smallest configuration, colloquially known as a "balloon" oak. Normal oaks can also generate in the <a href="/w/Trial_chambers" class="mw-redirect" title="Trial chambers">trial chambers</a> and they're all the same type with a single <a href="/w/Dirt" title="Dirt">dirt</a> underneath and a single <a href="/w/Water" title="Water">water</a> next to it. When near <a href="/w/Flowers" class="mw-redirect" title="Flowers">flowers</a> oak trees may generate with a <a href="/w/Bee_nest" class="mw-redirect" title="Bee nest">bee nest</a>.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Spruce">Spruce</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=6&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Spruce" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section's source code: Spruce"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Spruce" title="Spruce">Spruce</a></div>
<p>Spruce trees grow from spruce saplings and have growth patterns and requirements similar to birch trees, although they appear different. They are mainly found in the <a href="/w/Taiga" title="Taiga">taiga</a> biome, but they may also generate in <a href="/w/Windswept_forest" class="mw-redirect" title="Windswept forest">windswept forest</a>, <a href="/w/Snowy_plains" class="mw-redirect" title="Snowy plains">snowy plains</a>, <a href="/w/Snowy_taiga" class="mw-redirect" title="Snowy taiga">snowy taiga</a>, and <a href="/w/Old_growth_taiga" class="mw-redirect mw-disambig" title="Old growth taiga">old growth taiga</a> biomes. 
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Birch">Birch</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=7&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Birch" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section's source code: Birch"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Birch" title="Birch">Birch</a></div>
<p>Birch trees look fairly similar to small oaks in terms of height and are most commonly found in <a href="/w/Birch_forest" class="mw-redirect" title="Birch forest">birch forest</a> biomes. There are two types of birch: a shorter tree that can be grown by the player with birch saplings; and a taller, rarer variety that generates only naturally in <a href="/w/Old_Growth_Birch_Forest" title="Old Growth Birch Forest">old growth birch forest</a> biomes. When near <a href="/w/Flowers" class="mw-redirect" title="Flowers">flowers</a> birch trees may generate with a <a href="/w/Bee_nest" class="mw-redirect" title="Bee nest">bee nest</a>.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Jungle">Jungle</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=8&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Jungle" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section's source code: Jungle"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main articles: <a href="/w/Jungle_tree" class="mw-redirect" title="Jungle tree">Jungle tree</a> and <a href="/w/Jungle_Bush" title="Jungle Bush">Jungle Bush</a></div>
<p>Jungle trees are one of the rarest naturally generated trees in Minecraft because they are native to the <a href="/w/Jungle" title="Jungle">jungle</a> biomes, which are themselves rare. When planted in grass or dirt they grow into a jungle tree with a 1×1 trunk, but the <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">player</a> can place them in a 2×2 formation to grow a large jungle tree with a 2×2 trunk like the trees found naturally in the jungle biome. Jungle bushes also generate in the jungle biome, featuring a single jungle log surrounded by oak leaves. Jungle bushes cannot be grown by a player.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Acacia">Acacia</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=9&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Acacia" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=9" title="Edit section's source code: Acacia"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Acacia" title="Acacia">Acacia</a></div>
<p>Acacias are found in the <a href="/w/Savanna" title="Savanna">savanna</a> biome. They are about 8 blocks tall and feature diagonal trunks, and may occasionally have multiple canopies.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Dark_oak">Dark oak</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=10&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Dark oak" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=10" title="Edit section's source code: Dark oak"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Dark_oak" class="mw-redirect" title="Dark oak">Dark oak</a></div>
<p>Dark oaks are found in the <a href="/w/Dark_forest" class="mw-redirect" title="Dark forest">dark forest</a> biome. They have thick 2×2 trunks and require 4 saplings placed in the same configuration to be grown by a player. A dark oak always generates with dirt blocks under its trunk, even on a steep cliff. Irregular logs, representing large branches, are nearly always present and connected to the trunk. The canopy of a dark oak filters enough light that a dense forest of them is sufficiently dark for hostile mobs to spawn during the daytime.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Azalea">Azalea</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=11&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Azalea" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section's source code: Azalea"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Azalea_Tree" title="Azalea Tree">Azalea Tree</a></div>
<p>Azalea trees can generate on any empty space above a <a href="/w/Lush_cave" class="mw-redirect" title="Lush cave">lush cave</a>, with roots consisting of <a href="/w/Rooted_dirt" class="mw-redirect" title="Rooted dirt">rooted dirt</a> and <a href="/w/Hanging_roots" class="mw-redirect" title="Hanging roots">hanging roots</a> that reach down to the lush cave. The tree usually appears at the surface, but they can generate inside caves if there is enough room and a lush cave below.
</p><p>Azalea trees can be manually grown by applying bone meal to an <a href="/w/Azalea" title="Azalea">azalea</a> or <a href="/w/Flowering_azalea" class="mw-redirect" title="Flowering azalea">flowering azalea</a> block ("bush"). Unlike most trees, they do not have their own wood type (the trunks are composed of oak logs), but they have two types of leaf block: <a href="/w/Azalea_leaves" class="mw-redirect" title="Azalea leaves">azalea leaves</a>, and <a href="/w/Flowering_azalea_leaves" class="mw-redirect" title="Flowering azalea leaves">flowering azalea leaves</a>.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Mangrove">Mangrove</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=12&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Mangrove" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section's source code: Mangrove"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Mangrove" title="Mangrove">Mangrove</a></div>
<p>Mangroves are found in muddy <a href="/w/Mangrove_swamp" class="mw-redirect" title="Mangrove swamp">mangrove swamps</a>, growing in water or on land. They are grown from <a href="/w/Propagule" class="mw-redirect" title="Propagule">propagules</a>, which can be found hanging from the trees. A mangrove converts any mud below its roots to <a href="/w/Muddy_mangrove_roots" class="mw-redirect" title="Muddy mangrove roots">muddy mangrove roots</a>. The wood has a deep red-orange color.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Cherry">Cherry</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=13&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Cherry" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=13" title="Edit section's source code: Cherry"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Cherry" title="Cherry">Cherry</a></div><p>
Cherry trees are found in <a href="/w/Cherry_grove" class="mw-redirect" title="Cherry grove">cherry groves</a>. They have distinct pink leaves and horizontally facing branches. They also have a unique petal falling particle effect. They may occasionally have multiple canopies. When near <a href="/w/Flowers" class="mw-redirect" title="Flowers">flowers</a> they may generate with a <a href="/w/Bee_nest" class="mw-redirect" title="Bee nest">bee nest</a>.</p><ul class="gallery mw-gallery-traditional">

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Pale_Oak">Pale Oak</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=14&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Pale Oak" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=14" title="Edit section's source code: Pale Oak"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Pale_Oak" title="Pale Oak">Pale Oak</a></div><p>
Pale oaks are found in <a href="/w/Pale_garden" class="mw-redirect" title="Pale garden">pale gardens</a>. They have thick 2×2 trunks and gray leaves with a leaf-shaped falling particle effect. They generate with <a href="/w/Pale_hanging_moss" class="mw-redirect" title="Pale hanging moss">pale hanging moss</a> on some leaves, naturally generated pale oaks also may contain a <a href="/w/Creaking_heart" class="mw-redirect" title="Creaking heart">creaking heart</a>.</p><ul class="gallery mw-gallery-traditional">

<p>Poplars are found in <a href="/w/Dappled_forest" class="mw-redirect" title="Dappled forest">dappled forests</a>. They can generate or grow with red, orange, or yellow <a href="/w/Leaves" title="Leaves">leaves</a>. <a href="/w/Shelf_mushrooms" class="mw-redirect" title="Shelf mushrooms">Shelf mushrooms</a> sometimes generate on the trunk.

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Variant_trees">Variant trees</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=16&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Variant trees" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=16" title="Edit section's source code: Variant trees"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Some trees can generate as one of the two following variants of the normal tree. Both of these generate naturally, while only dying trees can be grown out of normal saplings.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Fallen_trees">Fallen trees</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=17&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Fallen trees" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=17" title="Edit section's source code: Fallen trees"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Fallen_Tree" title="Fallen Tree">Fallen Tree</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Fallen_Logs.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Fallen_Logs.jpg/300px-Fallen_Logs.jpg?9da8c" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="120" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Fallen_Logs.jpg/600px-Fallen_Logs.jpg?9da8c 2x" data-file-width="1683" data-file-height="674"></a><figcaption>The different fallen tree types</figcaption></figure>

</p><p>These trees consist of a single upright log, or stump. Logs lying on their side are often found 1–2 blocks from the stump and can have mushrooms growing from them.

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Trees_with_vines">Trees with vines</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=18&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Trees with vines" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=18" title="Edit section's source code: Trees with vines"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Tree_with_Vines" title="Tree with Vines">Tree with Vines</a></div><div class="msgbox searchaux msgbox-mini msgbox-blue" style="max-width: 50em;">

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Dying_trees.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Dying_trees.png/300px-Dying_trees.png?0606b" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Dying_trees.png/600px-Dying_trees.png?0606b 2x" data-file-width="3840" data-file-height="2160"></a><figcaption>All trees with vines</figcaption></figure>
<p>These trees have the standard growth pattern of any other tree, however, all exposed logs in the main trunk are covered with <a href="/w/Vines" title="Vines">vines</a>. They can generate as dark oak, jungle, spruce, or small oak trees, or can grow from saplings.

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Foliage_colors">Foliage colors</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=19&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Foliage colors" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=19" title="Edit section's source code: Foliage colors"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Color#Biome_colors" class="mw-disambig" title="Color">Color § Biome colors</a></div>
<p>Depending on the <a href="/w/Biome" title="Biome">biome</a> the tree is located, the color of the leaves may differ. For example, if an oak is in a colder biome, such as a taiga or windswept hills biome, it has a blue-green hue. However, if it is in a dry biome, such as a desert or savanna, it has a mustard yellow hue. Spruce, birch, azalea, cherry, pale oak, and poplar leaves do not follow these rules; they always have the same color regardless of the biome. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, biome-tinted leaves turn white during <a href="/w/Snowfall" title="Snowfall">snowfall</a>.
</p>

<p>Leaves are checked individually for biome coloration rather than as part of a larger tree; as such, trees that were grown between biomes usually have multiple shades on each side.
</p>

<p>Issues relating to "Tree" are maintained on the <a href="/w/Bug_tracker" title="Bug tracker">bug tracker</a>. Issues should be reported and viewed <a target="_blank" rel="nofollow noreferrer noopener" class="external text" href="https://bugs.mojang.com/issues/?jql=project%20in%20%28MC%2C%20MCPE%29%20AND%20%28resolution%20is%20EMPTY%20OR%20resolution%20in%20%281%2C%202%2C%206%29%29%20AND%20%28summary%20~%20%22Tree%22%29%20ORDER%20BY%20resolution%20DESC">there</a>.

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Trivia">Trivia</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=32&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Trivia" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=32" title="Edit section's source code: Trivia"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<ul><li>Floating trees may appear when small above-ground lava lakes generate in a forested area.<sup id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This happens since the tree is generated when the <a href="/w/Chunk" title="Chunk">chunk</a> loads first, before the lake appears underneath. This leaves the tree floating above the lake, causing the tree to catch fire, potentially spreading to other trees and starting a forest fire.</li></ul>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Publicity">Publicity</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Tree?section=33&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Publicity" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Tree?action=edit&section=33" title="Edit section's source code: Publicity"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<ul><li>In the mid-2010s, the action of chopping a tree was referenced in a <i><a href="/w/Honey_Nut_Cheerios" class="mw-redirect" title="Honey Nut Cheerios">Honey Nut Cheerios</a></i> advertisement. In the ad, it is represented by stacks of cheerios, and broken using a <a href="/w/Pickaxe" title="Pickaxe">pickaxe</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-10"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li>Trees resembling oak and azalea appear in a <i>Minecraft</i>-like scene in the game <i><a href="/w/Happy_Color" class="mw-redirect" title="Happy Color">Happy Color</a></i>.</li>
<li>A single oak tree appears in <i><a href="/w/Choplifter_HD" class="mw-redirect" title="Choplifter HD">Choplifter HD</a></i>. It uses textures for oak leaves and logs, but is depicted in a radically different shape, being much taller and sporadic.</li>
<li>Several spruce and oak trees appear in the Games Ending of <a href="/w/The_Stanley_Parable" title="The Stanley Parable">The Stanley Parable</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li></ul>
